summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on application integration: SDK usage, tool/function calling, and producing structured JSON outputs for downstream systems. Reviewed pilot results (latency/cost tradeoffs), discussed mapping function schemas to product events, and agreed next steps to run integration tests and provide SDK examples.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, on the calendar today POC weekly sync, mostly SDK and the function calling integration work. Markus, Sara, Evan, you good?
[00:08] Markus Lee: Yeah sounds good, sorry a bit delayed, pulled up the results from last week.
[00:12] Sara Gomez: All good here. Quick agenda — results, tuning notes, then integration questions on structured output.
[00:18] Priya Rao: Quick note, I pushed an update to the SDK example repo, the snippet now shows a function call and a sample schema return. It's in the shared drive link.
[00:26] Evan Patel: Got it, saw that. We tried the hosted endpoint and saw about 420ms median per request for the summary flow, with ~2.1k tokens per minute cost estimate. The P50 and P95 were a bit bumpy during bursts.
[00:36] Alex Chen: Right, and that's with default batching. For your workload which is short doc summaries we recommended smaller batch windows to keep latency predictable. Did you run with the streaming option?
[00:44] Markus Lee: We turned streaming on; results a little noisy. The client needs a deterministic JSON object, so streaming partial tokens made parsing tricky.
[00:52] Priya Rao: Makes sense — two approaches: either stream plain text then parse at the end, or use function calling/structured output so model returns a single JSON blob. The SDK snippet uses the function-calling feature to return {event_type, summary_text, risk_flags}.
[01:06] Sara Gomez: That's exactly what we want. Can you show the schema mapping again? We want to map event_type to our internal enums.
[01:12] Priya Rao: Sure, in the snippet the function signature is: name: "create_event", parameters: {"type": "object", "properties": {"event_type": {"type":"string"}, "summary_text": {"type":"string"}, "risk_flags": {"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}}, "required":["event_type","summary_text"]}. Note — transcription might mangle quotes in the shared doc, I'll send a clean copy.
[01:30] Evan Patel: Cool. One thing we hit — when the model returns function calls we get an extra wrapper in the response object that our current parser wasn't expecting. Slight mismatch between SDK and our lambda.
[01:40] Alex Chen: That's common. We have two recommended patterns: 1) have Redwood's SDK handle function call resolution and return the JSON payload directly to your app, or 2) accept the raw response and run a small adapter layer. Which would you prefer?
[01:52] Markus Lee: We prefer minimal adapters; let the SDK give us the final JSON. Less glue code.
[01:56] Priya Rao: Ok we'll provide an example where SDK handles the function call and returns the parsed JSON. Also will demonstrate retry semantics for transient errors and how to preserve the original prompt for debugging.
[02:08] Sara Gomez: On the results front — we saw a ~4% quality regression vs baseline in the multi-doc concat summaries for one user cohort, do you think that's model drift or prompt mismatch?
[02:16] Priya Rao: Could be prompt framing — we changed the system role to be more aggressive. Suggest we run A/B with the older prompt, and pin a model variant while we tune. Redwood supports pinning model versions and we can do canary rollouts so you can measure quality metrics.
[02:30] Alex Chen: Also quantization profile matters — the smaller int8 variants save cost but can slightly change output patterns. For critical outputs we recommend the 16-bit-ish profile for now or run evals.
[02:42] Evan Patel: Network question — if we move to dedicated or private, what's the path for VPC peering and KMS integration? We need to ensure keys never leave our account.
[02:50] Priya Rao: For Private deployment we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integration; for VPC we do peering or private-link depending on cloud. I'll send the topology doc. For dedicated we can overlay with customer VPC and control egress points. Note that some features like streaming over private links have small setup steps.
[03:06] Markus Lee: Great. Back to integration — we attempted to use the SDK's structured output helper but hit a serializer error when risk_flags is empty array; the SDK returned null.
[03:16] Priya Rao: That's a bug in the older SDK build 0.9.2; we patched it in 0.9.5 to normalize empty arrays to []. I'll include the release notes and the fixed snippet.
[03:26] Alex Chen: For testing, Priya can provision a short-lived dedicated-rt endpoint with 2xA100-equivalent to reproduce your latency and throughput; that will show P95 under load. We can also run a token-cost estimate.
[03:40] Evan Patel: That would be useful; real network path matters.
[03:44] Sara Gomez: On verification — we'll run 50 sample records through the end-to-end path: ingestion -> SDK call -> function response -> downstream event store. We'll capture latencies and token counts.
[03:56] Markus Lee: One more thing — how do we handle partial failures? If the model returns an unparsable JSON for create_event, what's the recommended retry/backoff and alerting pattern?
[04:06] Priya Rao: Standard pattern: 1) if unparsable, log raw response to S3 (retaining context IDs), 2) increment a failure metric and run a lightweight verifier (schema validator). For retries, use exponential backoff up to 3 tries then bubble to DLQ. We'll add sample code.
[04:20] Alex Chen: We'll also provide a small evaluation harness so you can run batches of examples through the pinned model variant and get pass/fail counts for schema compliance.
[04:30] Evan Patel: Security note — we need SOC2 docs and data retention policy for hosted flows. Do you have the docs?
[04:36] Alex Chen: Yes, I'll send SOC2 and the data retention export. For POC we can enable short retention and purge logs.
[04:42] Sara Gomez: About telemetry — can we get per-request token breakdowns? That helps product cost modeling.
[04:46] Priya Rao: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token and latency per route and per model, and we can give a demo of the console. But for the POC we'll share CSV exports of the test runs.
[04:56] Markus Lee: Any blockers on our side? We need the SDK snippet with function call handling and the dedicated endpoint.
[05:02] Alex Chen: We'll get both. Priya will do the endpoint. I'll send the snippet and security docs.
[05:08] Priya Rao: I'll also add a small Node and Python example showing how to register the function schema and get back the parsed JSON from the SDK. Also include sample unit tests for schema validation.
[05:20] Sara Gomez: Perfect. Timeline — we'll run tests by next Monday and meet again to review.
[05:24] Alex Chen: Next sync 2025-02-19 same time, unless you need earlier.
[05:28] Markus Lee: Same time works. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
[05:32] Alex Chen: Thanks all, action items recap: Alex send SDK + security, Priya set up endpoint, Markus/Evan run tests. Bye.
[05:38] [call end]
